question.problem:
$$
V=\text{Span}{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]},\,B={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]}
$$

Consider the subspace $V$ and an orthogonal basis $B$ of $V,$ given above. Given that $B$ is derived from $V$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, what is the value of $\frac{a}{b}?$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's denote 

$\,$ ${a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ 

We proceed to find an orthogonal basis using the Gram-Schmidt process, as follows.

**Step 1**: We set ${v}_{1}={a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$

**Step 2**: Next, we find ${v}_{2}$, by using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{2} & ={a}_{2}-\frac{{a}_{2}\cdot {v}_{1}}{{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}}{v}_{1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the formula for ${v}_{2}$ in our case gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{2} & ={a}_{2}-\frac{3\cdot 1+2\cdot 1+2\cdot (-2)}{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}{v}_{1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{17}{6} \\ \frac{11}{6} \\ \frac{7}{3}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $B={{v}_{1},{v}_{2}}={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}\frac{17}{6} \\ \frac{11}{6} \\ \frac{7}{3}\end{aligned}]}$ is an orthogonal basis for $V.$

Finally, we have $a=\frac{17}{6},$ $b=\frac{11}{6},$ and 

$$
\frac{a}{b}=\frac{(\frac{17}{6})}{(\frac{11}{6})}=\frac{17}{11}.
$$
